I apologise for all the mug related content I’ve posting recently… my feed here tends to reflect what it is that I’m doing in the studio and well, these simple mugs have been at the forefront of my craft for the past two weeks. There are hundreds of the damn pots slowly drying beneath plastic at the moment, I board them up in a wrapping of plastic sheeting and slot them over the radiators to gradually turn bone dry, this way cracks in the handles joins practically never occur. Slow and even drying is key. If instead I pulled a batch of handles and just left the board out in the open on my workbench, I’m pretty certain they’d all simply crack off. I adore the repetition by the way, for mugs especially, they’re simple enough to not feel intimidating, and they provide a good balance of techniques: throwing, trimming and finally handling pulling. They’re as close to a mantra as I get with this craft and they’re perhaps the only shape where I feel any sense of ‘mindfulness’ as I create them, (I normally dislike this term in relation to pottery), but with these I can simply let my hands get on with the job whilst my ears are following along to my audiobook, hands occupied, mind occupied and the hours pass in a flash. #pottery #mug #wheelthrownpottery #asmr #craftsmanship #maker #studiopottery

lidded jar tutorial - part 1 (throwing the jar body and lid)✨ have to break this up into 3 parts because it will take weeks to go through the steps (we're making these jars in real time and rely on a community studio to fire) and I simply can't fit throwing, trimming, and glazing the jars into one reel 🥲 i find 200g is perfect for throwing the small jar body, plus another 150g for the lid. you'll see i throw my jar body and lid separately, leaving a lot of the refining for the trimming stage. especially with the lids, I find it easier to throw them roughly and finesse the fit once they're leather hard. i don't wire off the lids or jars, i wait until they pop off the bats. xo shan #pottery #potterytutorial #liddedjar #handmadeceramics #canadianartist

I have a bit of an exaggerated skirt on this piece so I can show you a couple techniques for removing the skirt from the base of your cylinder. Removing it twice requires a bit of extra clay. In addition new potters who have not yet learned to bring clay up their piece frequently find that there is quite a bit to remove at the end of throwing their piece so this is a reflection of what a beginner might have on the wheel after working hard to bring clay up into the wall. It’s such a common groan from students at Twisted Clay when I tell them to cut their skirt away. They are so worried about ruining the pot as it can be tricky to get your head around, but once you do, you won’t want to skip this step ever again. Not a member of my online studio yet? videos.caption: Throwing a Donut on the Wheel Center your clay and compress it into a wide, flat puck. Poke through the center down to the wheel head and slowly stretch it open to create the donut hole. Split the ring 50/50—leave a base slightly thicker than your future walls. Pull up the inner wall first, then the outer wall. Join the walls together. It doesn’t matter which one overlaps—adjust based on how the clay moves. Before joining, I thin out the edges to avoid a step at the seam. Important! Remove any slip and excess water from the seam—otherwise, it will crack during drying or firing. Once the walls are joined, the trapped air inside acts as a support structure, allowing you to refine the shape and compress the seam. Trim the excess clay inside and out, and your donut is ready! Follow me for more wheel-throwing tips! … … #ceramics #potteryvideos #pottery #fyp #usa
